extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and KIPO examiners handling requests for expedited examination (Korean IP filings)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, evidentiary requirements, and eligibility criteria for requesting and determining expedited examination of patent and utility model applications at the Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO), including special categories (start-ups, component/material businesses, award-winning inventions), electronic commerce, PPH and PCT-PPH pathways, and required supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Component & material technology business - acceptance without evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications from component & material technology development businesses shall be accepted as the invention being practiced or prepared to be practiced as a business without submission of the above-mentioned evidential documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This refers to Article 6 of the Enforcement Rule of the Act on Special Measure for the Promotion of Specialized Enterprises, etc. If an application is by a confirmed component & material business, expedited examination may be granted on the assumption the invention is being practiced, without the usual proving documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevancy determination for parts/materials-specialized businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: The relevancy between parts·materials-specialized businesses and the claimed invention shall be determined based on proving documents (business license, and etc.) enclosed in the expedited examination request form, and if necessary, by referring to the total information network run by the Korea Institute for Advancement of Technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the relevancy cannot be checked or confirmed, the examiner may order the requester to supplement the proving documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint application with a component & material business
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is jointly filed and one of the applicants is a component & material technology development business, the request for expedited examination on the application shall be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request is accepted only when the company confirmed as a component & material technology development business and the name of the applicant are (appropriately) identified; see related provisions for venture companies (mutatis mutandis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirement for component & material business status
rubrics_metrics.description: At one point among the filing date of a patent application, the date of request for expedited examination or the date of determination on expedited examination, an application shall be a component & material technology development business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must hold the qualifying business confirmation at least at one of those key dates to be considered under this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable evidential documents for component & material businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidential documents of component & material technology development business shall be the original copy of the confirmation of component & material technology development business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a copy of the confirmation is deeded to be identical with the original copy, the copy shall be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarded-in-contest inventions with government financial support - acceptance without proving documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application with respect to an invention awarded in an open contest or competition hosted/run by the government or a local government, which is financially supported by the government or a local government for commercialization or for filing of a patent application, shall be accepted for expedited examination on the assumption that it is being practiced or to be practiced, without submission of any proving documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when the invention both (a) was awarded in a government-hosted contest and (b) is financially supported by government/local government for commercialization or filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of award/financial-support relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of whether an application is relevant to an invention selected in an open contest or competition shall be based on an expedited request form and enclosed proving documents (a certificate of merit, a certificate, a confirmation, and etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An invention selected in an open contest or competition can include creative idea or art. If all inventions awarded in a contest are known to be beneficiaries of commercialization or patent filing and that fact can be proved by other means, the specific proving documents need not be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start-up financial support thresholds for expedited acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application financially supported by the government with over 10 million won for technology development/commercialization, or filed by early-stage startups funded by venture capital/cloud funding/angel investors/accelerators with over 50 million won, shall be accepted for expedited examination without submission of proving documents, on the assumption that the claimed invention is being practiced or to be practiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is pursuant to relevant domestic support acts (Support for SME Establishment Act; Business Start-up Support Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of start-up status and required proving documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of whether a patent application is filed by a start-up shall be based on an expedited examination request form and any proving documents, for example, a business license proving an early stage startup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable proving documents: agreements/affirmation documents/project implementation confirmations/final evaluation confirmations for government-funded projects; investment performance certificates/confirmations/commitments for venture/cloud/angel/accelerator funding over the stated thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint application name mismatch - proving document timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When a joint patent application has different names between the business and the patent applicant, the time period to determine proving documents shall follow the rules for a patent application filed by a business confirmed as a parts·materials-specialized business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the clause '⑤ a patent application filed by a business which was confirmed as a parts․materials-specialized business' for timing and documentary rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications directly related to electronic commerce - subject categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications related to electronic commerce which promotes electronic transactions under Article 2 of the Framework Act on Electronic Commerce: (i) transaction methods (auctions, reverse auctions, advertisement, education, etc.), (ii) electronic money and payment technologies (IC card type, network-based electronic money, cyber coin, online bank account transactions, credit card payment methods), (iii) security or verification technologies (network access blocking, transaction verification, electronic signature, smart cards), and (iv) other technologies recognized as necessary for promotion of electronic transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also includes technology developed by government or government-funded centers for active promotion of electronic trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic commerce definition guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation guidance: 'electronic document' means any information prepared, transmitted, received or stored in electronic form by an information processing system; 'electronic commerce' means any transaction where whole or part of goods/services transaction is made through electronic documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should ensure the application is related to electronic transaction as defined under the Framework Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility via KIPO–foreign patent office agreement (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application for which KIPO Commissioner has agreed with the Commissioner of a foreign patent office to expedite examination (participating countries list provided) is eligible if it falls under enumerated conditions (e.g., earliest filing/priority date matches and other specific requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participating countries include Japan, US, Denmark, UK, Canada, Russia, EU/EPO, China, etc.; conditions differ by agreement type and are set out in sub-clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility when earlier filing in JPO and foreign search report available
rubrics_metrics.description: All conditions must be fulfilled: (1) After a patent application is first filed with the JPO, the same invention is filed with KIPO; (2) A search report relevant to the JPO-filed application can be obtained from a foreign patent office or an inter-governmental office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when relying on prior art/search results obtained from the Japanese office or intergovernmental organizations; evidentiary support required as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility when corresponding application has at least one claim indicated allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application is eligible where the corresponding application filed with a participating patent office has at least one claim indicated allowable in a most recent office action for examination, and where the concerned KIPO application’s claims are identical to the allowable claims or narrowed by restricting or adding limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision facilitates expedited examination when a foreign office has indicated allowability; claim correspondence must be demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents when prior art search report from foreign office is relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: When a prior art search report related to the concerned patent application is obtained from a foreign patent office or intergovernmental organization, the requester shall submit: (1) a copy of the prior art search report from the foreign office/organization, (2) a copy of prior art documents indicated in that report (non-patent documents must be submitted), and (3) a detailed explanation comparing the claimed invention and the disclosure of the prior art document specifying differences and possible technical effects (specify cited parts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior art search reports prepared by the requester or by an external agency at the requester's initiative are NOT recognized as reports obtained from foreign offices and thus are not acceptable; if the explanation is insufficient, examiner can order supplementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) basic eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPH allows an applicant who received a positive decision on claims from the Office of First Filing (OFF) — that at least one claim is allowable — to request expedited examination at the Office of Second Filing (OSF) for the corresponding application that includes claims identical to the allowable claims or narrowed by restrictions/additions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participating country lists and program participation should be checked on KIPO homepage as participating countries can change; eased requirements since Jan 1, 2014 allow eligibility when earliest priority dates match.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH: what counts as 'claims decided allowable'
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims decided allowable are: (a) claims indicated allowable in a written decision to grant a patent; (b) in the absence of a written decision, claims indicated allowable in the most recent office action or decision to reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If allowability is not explicit because the participating office did not indicate a ground for rejection, it may be deemed allowable but the petitioner should explain a suitable reason in a written document. If the participating-office-app with patentable claims is not the one serving as the basis of priority claim, the requester must explain the relation between that application and the one serving as basis of priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH: all-claims correspondence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims of the concerned patent application shall correspond to the claims decided allowable in a patent application filed in a participating country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence means substantially identical claims or claims further limited by adding limitations. Differences only in translation or claim types (independent/dependent) may be treated as substantially same. Different claim categories count as non-corresponding. Claim correspondence is determined based on a claim correspondence table submitted by the requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH evidential documents (Annex Form and evidence list)
rubrics_metrics.description: A PPH requester shall file a written explanation referencing Annexed Form no. 3 and submit: (a) copy of the claims including those recognized as allowable by the participating office; (b) copy of an examination-related notification on the corresponding patent application issued by the participating office; (c) copy of prior arts relied upon in that notification (non-patent docs must be submitted); (d) explanation on correspondence between each claim and the allowable claims (claim correspondence table) — the correspondence explanation must be submitted in any case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner can obtain documents via public networks (AIPN, PAIR, PVS online), submission may not be necessary. If documents are in non-Korean/English languages, translations must be submitted unless examiner can obtain translations via networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT-PPH eligibility and claim correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the PCT-PPH, a request for expedited examination is allowed where an international search or international preliminary examination on the corresponding international application includes claims meeting requirements for novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability, and all claims of the concerned national application correspond to those claims (substantially identical or further limited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence is judged by a claim correspondence table submitted by the requester; mere differences in translations or claim types are acceptable as identical; different claim categories negate correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT-PPH evidential documents (Annex Form and evidence list)
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester under PCT-PPH shall submit (using Annexed Form no. 6): (a) copy of patent claims decided to meet requirements in an international search/IPER/WO opinions; (b) copy of the written opinion(s) or international preliminary examination report; (c) copy of prior art documents cited in those international opinions/reports (non-patent docs must be submitted); (d) explanation on correspondence between all claims of concerned application and the claims recognized as meeting requirements (claim correspondence explanation must be submitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'opinions on an international application' (Box VIII) indicate ambiguity/unclear claims, the requester must explain that all claims are not affected (e.g., provide responses or amendments). If such explanations are not provided, examiner may order amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination/redetermination instructions and amendment consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining expedited examination for applications agreed between KIPO and foreign offices, the result of determination is not notified to requester unless rejected. If an applicant amends claims after determination in ways not reflected in prior explanations (e.g., claims not included in prior comparison or not substantially identical), the examiner may order corrections and re-determine whether to permit expedited examination, granting up to one month to correct at examiner's discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant submits comparison explanations covering amended claims or correspondence explanations for claims meeting international requirements, expedited examination shall proceed without re-determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art documents: patent vs non-patent handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When prior art/patent documents cited in foreign reports/notifications are patent documents, examiners can usually obtain them and submission may not be required; where cited prior art are non-patent documents, requester is obliged to submit the concerned non-patent documents, otherwise the examiner may order their submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule applies across foreign-search-report-based requests, PPH and PCT-PPH evidentiary requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable source of prior art search reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art search reports recognized are those prepared by a foreign patent office or an intergovernmental organization (e.g., prior art cited in an office action of a foreign patent office, PCT international search report, EPO prior art search report); reports prepared by the requester or by an external agency at the requester's initiative are NOT recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unrecognized reports are submitted, the examiner shall order correction of the request for expedited examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation requirements for evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where evidential documents are written in a language other than Korean or English, their translation shall be submitted together. If an examiner can obtain an English or Korean translation through an information communication network, the translation need not be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same rule applies to PPH and PCT-PPH evidentiary documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim correspondence table requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether claims correspond to each other shall be determined based on a claim correspondence table that a requester submits with a written explanation of request for expedited examination; an explanation on claim correspondence must be submitted in any case (PPH/PCT-PPH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds for correspondence must be indicated for each claim (e.g., statement that claims are literal translations or explain mere translation differences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of 'opinions on an international application' (Box VIII) in PCT-PPH
rubrics_metrics.description: If 'opinions on an international application' are indicated in Box No. VIII of an international written opinion/IPER, the requester must explain the intention that all claims of the concerned patent application are not affected by those opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanations may include responses to the opinions or show that irregularities are addressed through amendments; otherwise, the examiner may order amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model registration filed/requested for expedited examination within two months - (eligibility note)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application of utility model registration that was requested for examination upon filing and then requested for expedited examination within two months from the filing date: a patent application shall not be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text is prescriptive: additional evidential documents do not need to be submitted. (Note: the directive also explains basic characteristics of utility models — 10-year term and eligibility for expedited examination when requested — and treats utility models differently from patents; refer to full directive for exact applicability/conditions.)
